cultural_context.description: West Bengal has a diverse cultural heritage expressed through Bengali language and literature, classical and folk music and dance, festivals, religious traditions, crafts, textiles, cuisine, theatre, and the historic and cultural life of Kolkata and other regions of the state.
cultural_context.important_note: Cultural practices vary across regions, communities, religions, families, generations, and individual contexts. Information in this file should not be treated as universal to every person in West Bengal.

source.organization: Department of Tourism, Government of West Bengal
source.title: West Bengal Tourism

communication_guidance: Use respectful communication when interacting with local people.
West Bengal has linguistic, religious, regional, and community diversity, so do not assume one communication style represents everyone.
Kolkata is particularly diverse and should not be treated as representative of every part of West Bengal.
When participating in a cultural or religious event, follow the guidance of local hosts, organizers, or the relevant venue.
greetings_and_communication.limitation: The current verified knowledge base does not contain a sufficiently sourced everyday Bengali phrase list. Do not invent Bengali phrases or translations.

verified_information.description: Official West Bengal tourism material identifies Bengali cuisine as an important part of the state's cultural experience and documents regional food traditions.

source.organization: Department of Tourism, Government of West Bengal
source.title: West Bengal Tourism

verified_information.description: Kolkata has a well-documented culinary heritage that forms part of the city's broader cultural identity.

source.organization: Department of Tourism, Government of West Bengal
source.title: Kolkata

dining_guidance: Do not assume Kolkata cuisine represents all of West Bengal.
Food practices can vary according to region, religion, community, family tradition, and individual preference.
Respect individual dietary choices and follow local hosts' guidance at traditional meals and community events.
food_and_dining.limitation: The verified knowledge base does not establish universal everyday dining etiquette for every region and community in West Bengal.

core_values.name: Literary and artistic heritage
core_values.description: West Bengal has a strong documented heritage in literature, music, dance, theatre, visual arts, crafts, and cultural festivals.

source.organization: Ministry of Tourism, Government of India
source.title: West Bengal

core_values.name: Regional and community diversity
core_values.description: West Bengal includes distinct cultural regions and communities, including the Himalayan area, the plains, and coastal and forest regions. Cultural practices therefore differ significantly across locations.

source.organization: Department of Tourism, Government of West Bengal
source.title: West Bengal Tourism

festivals.name: Durga Puja
festivals.description: Durga Puja is one of West Bengal's most prominent cultural festivals, especially associated with Kolkata and other parts of the state. It includes elaborate public celebrations, artistic installations, rituals, music, and community participation.

source.organization: Ministry of Culture, Government of India
source.title: Durga Puja in Kolkata

festivals.name: Poila Boishakh
festivals.period: Usually April 14 or 15; date follows the Bengali calendar
festivals.description: Poila Boishakh is the Bengali New Year and is celebrated with cultural programs, family observances, traditional foods, and other regional customs.

source.organization: Department of Tourism, Government of West Bengal
source.title: West Bengal Tourism

festivals.name: Kali Puja
festivals.description: Kali Puja is an important religious festival in West Bengal and is observed with worship and community celebrations.

source.organization: Department of Tourism, Government of West Bengal
source.title: West Bengal Tourism

festivals.name: Poush Mela
festivals.description: Poush Mela is a cultural fair associated with Santiniketan and includes music, crafts, performances, and community participation.

source.organization: Ministry of Tourism, Government of India
source.title: Poush Mela

festivals.name: Gangasagar Mela
festivals.description: Gangasagar Mela is a major pilgrimage and cultural gathering held at Sagar Island, with religious observances and participation by pilgrims and visitors.

source.organization: Department of Tourism, Government of West Bengal
source.title: Gangasagar

festivals.name: Naba Barsha
festivals.period: Usually April; date follows the Bengali calendar
festivals.description: Naba Barsha is another name used for the Bengali New Year celebration and is associated with cultural and community observances.

source.organization: Department of Tourism, Government of West Bengal
source.title: West Bengal Tourism

traditional_dances.name: Chhau
traditional_dances.description: Chhau is a traditional dance tradition practiced in eastern India. Purulia Chhau is strongly associated with Purulia in West Bengal and uses vigorous movement, music, and elaborate masks.

source.organization: UNESCO
source.title: Chhau dance

traditional_dances.name: Gambhira
traditional_dances.description: Gambhira is a folk performance tradition associated with Malda and other areas of West Bengal, combining music, dance, dialogue, and social themes.

source.organization: Department of Tourism, Government of West Bengal
source.title: West Bengal Tourism

traditional_dances.name: Baul performance tradition
traditional_dances.description: Baul traditions combine music, spiritual expression, poetry, and performance and form an important part of Bengal's intangible cultural heritage.

source.organization: UNESCO
source.title: Baul songs

traditional_clothing.name: Traditional Bengali attire
traditional_clothing.description: Traditional clothing forms part of West Bengal's cultural and festival life. Sarees, dhotis, and regionally distinctive textiles are associated with traditional dress, but clothing varies by region, community, religion, occasion, and individual preference.

source.organization: Ministry of Tourism, Government of India
source.title: West Bengal

traditional_clothing.name: Baluchari saree
traditional_clothing.description: Baluchari sarees are a traditional handloom textile associated with Bishnupur in West Bengal and are known for woven narrative motifs.

source.organization: Ministry of Textiles, Government of India
source.title: Baluchari Saree

traditional_clothing.name: Tant handloom
traditional_clothing.description: Tant is a traditional Bengal handloom textile known for lightweight woven sarees and is associated with weaving traditions in West Bengal.

source.organization: Ministry of Textiles, Government of India
source.title: Tant Saree

traditional_arts.name: Kantha embroidery
traditional_arts.description: Kantha is a traditional textile embroidery practice associated with Bengal and is used to create decorative and functional embroidered textiles.

source.organization: Ministry of Textiles, Government of India
source.title: Kantha

traditional_arts.name: Dokra metal craft
traditional_arts.description: Dokra is a traditional lost-wax metal casting craft practiced in parts of West Bengal and other eastern Indian regions.

source.organization: Ministry of Textiles, Government of India
source.title: Dhokra Craft

traditional_arts.name: Terracotta of Bishnupur
traditional_arts.description: Bishnupur is known for terracotta art and architecture, including decorative terracotta work associated with its historic temples.

source.organization: Ministry of Tourism, Government of India
source.title: Bishnupur

traditional_arts.name: Patachitra
traditional_arts.description: Patachitra is a narrative painting tradition practiced in Bengal, particularly associated with scroll paintings and storytelling.

source.organization: Ministry of Textiles, Government of India
source.title: Patachitra

spiritual_and_cultural_practices.name: Durga Puja traditions
spiritual_and_cultural_practices.description: Durga Puja includes religious worship alongside large-scale artistic, musical, and community celebrations. UNESCO recognizes Durga Puja in Kolkata as intangible cultural heritage.

source.organization: UNESCO
source.title: Durga Puja in Kolkata

spiritual_and_cultural_practices.name: Baul spiritual tradition
spiritual_and_cultural_practices.description: Baul songs and traditions combine music, poetry, spiritual ideas, and a distinctive community-based cultural practice in Bengal.

source.organization: UNESCO
source.title: Baul songs

spiritual_and_cultural_practices.name: Pilgrimage traditions
spiritual_and_cultural_practices.description: Places such as Gangasagar have established pilgrimage traditions and large religious gatherings. Visitors should follow local instructions and respect religious practices.

source.organization: Department of Tourism, Government of West Bengal
source.title: Gangasagar

visitor_guidance: Treat temples, religious ceremonies, festivals, folk performances, and community celebrations with respect.
During Durga Puja and other large festivals, follow crowd-management, venue, photography, and safety instructions.
Ask before photographing people, ritual performers, religious ceremonies, or culturally significant activities when permission or local rules are unclear.
When entering temples or other sacred spaces, follow the venue's instructions regarding clothing, footwear, photography, and behavior.
Do not assume that Kolkata's cultural practices represent the entire state.
Do not generalize community-specific traditions such as Baul or Purulia Chhau to all residents of West Bengal.
Respect cultural and religious practices as living traditions rather than treating them simply as tourist entertainment.
West Bengal contains distinct Himalayan, plains, coastal, forest, and urban cultural contexts; adapt respectfully to the local setting.
